title: Coding benchmark task
description: Contract for benchmark/tasks/{split}/{task_id}/task.yaml. Defined by AGENT_BUILD_SPEC.md 5.1. Changing this file changes a contract - bump the version and say why in docs/decisions/.

id.description: snake_case, unique, and stable forever - it ends up in result files, so renaming one breaks historical comparisons. Must equal the task directory name.

category.description: Drives the category mix in 5.2. Do not invent new values without an ADR.

difficulty.description: easy = one file, obvious fix. medium = must run tests to localise. hard = multi-file, or the first plausible fix breaks something else.

split.description: Must match the parent directory. heldout is sealed once authored - see 5.4 rule 8.

instruction.description: What the agent is told. Describe the symptom, never the fix. Must not name a file under verification.test_files.

root.description: Fixed by the sandbox layout. Present so the contract is explicit in every task file.

loc.description: Non-blank, non-comment lines of Python under repo/. Capped at 500 by 5.4 rule 6 - this is a tool-use study, not a long-context study. Verified against a real count.

entrypoint_hint.description: Repo-relative path nudging the agent at the right file. Omit for hard tasks - localisation IS the task there.

runner.description: Only pytest for now. A second runner needs an ADR and a verifier change.

test_files.description: HIDDEN tests, task-dir-relative. Never mounted into the sandbox, never named in the instruction.

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock cap for the hidden suite. Keep small: this multiplies by 40 tasks x k samples on every eval.

n_tests.description: Real collected test count - validate_tasks.py enforces it against pytest --collect-only. At least 3 so partial credit is real (5.4 rule 5); reward_v1 is a fraction of this.

floor_tests.description: MEASURED reward floor, as a count: how many hidden tests already pass against the untouched repo, i.e. what a do-nothing agent scores. Optional and purely descriptive today - reward_v1 is unchanged and ADR 0006's normalisation is still Proposed. validate_tasks.py checks it when present and --fix-counts writes it, so it is a checked measurement rather than an author's guess. Headroom is n_tests - floor_tests; below ~6 the task discriminates poorly.

allowed_write_globs.description: Allow-list for write_file/edit_file. Must stay inside repo/ - anything else is a sandbox escape by definition.

forbidden_write_globs.description: Checked first and wins over the allow-list. Must include tests/** and solution/** - these are the reward-hacking surfaces from 5.7.

max_turns.description: Model turns before the episode is cut. Also a VRAM lever - see docs/vram_notes.md 3.2.

max_tool_calls.description: Total tool invocations before the episode is cut. Should exceed max_turns, since one turn may emit several calls.

source.description: 5.3 targets >=50% real_repo. Never label an invented bug as real_repo - that is an explicit never in 9.1.

license.description: Licence of the origin code, or of ours if authored. Permissive only - MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 / PSF-2.0 / CC0-1.0.

notes.description: How the task was derived. For real_repo, say exactly what was inverted or removed.

expected_files_changed.description: How many files the gold patch touches. Cross-checked against solution/gold.patch.

tags.description: Free-form labels for slicing results, e.g. off-by-one, mutable-default, packaging.
